bib.title: Fine-Tuning with Preference Alignment (LLM Engineer's Handbook, ch. 6)

question: How do you build a preference dataset and use DPO to align an SFT model to a target writing style?
contributions: Preference-dataset structure, size guidance and generation/evaluation methods
A pipeline building a 1,467-pair style preference set from blog extracts vs GPT-4o-mini generations
RLHF vs DPO overview and a Unsloth/TRL DPO run on TwinLlama-3.1-8B

method.summary: Builds a 1,467-pair preference dataset (blog extracts as chosen, GPT-4o-mini generations as rejected) and DPO-fine-tunes TwinLlama-3.1-8B with Unsloth/TRL and LoRA.

datasets.name: mlabonne/llmtwin-dpo
datasets.source: built from cleaned_documents.json blog articles; chosen = extracts, rejected = GPT-4o-mini output; on Hugging Face Hub
datasets.preprocessing: chunks of 1,000 to 2,000 chars split at sentence ends; filters: chosen >= 100 chars, uppercase start and ends in . ! ?; Alpaca template on prompt, EOS appended to answers

other.use: generates instructions, rejected answers and extracted answers; JSON mode, temperature 0.7, max_tokens 2000

training.objective: DPO (binary cross-entropy on preferred vs rejected, KL-anchored to reference)
training.batch_size: inferred: per_device_train_batch_size 2 x gradient_accumulation_steps 8 = 16 (single device not stated)
training.seq_len: inferred: max_length and max_prompt_length are each max_seq_length//2 with max_seq_length = 2048
training.precision: bf16 if supported else fp16; LoRA (QLoRA optional via load_in_4bit)
training.regularisation: beta 0.5 against reference (original model without adapters, ref_model=None)

other.lora_rank_alpha: prose says 64; printed code shows r=32, lora_alpha=32
other.eval: eval_strategy steps, eval_steps 0.2, eval batch size 2

metrics.name: Training/validation loss, rewards, margins, accuracies
metrics.definition: rewards = mean difference of log probabilities of trained and reference models; margins = chosen minus rejected rewards; accuracies = % of times chosen identified

eval.protocol: one qualitative sanity-check prompt; no benchmark scores

limits: The DPO outcome is one qualitative sample on one prompt; no quantitative evaluation in this chapter (stated: automating style evaluation is 'not the purpose of this chapter').
Prose says r and lora_alpha are raised to 64, but the printed code shows r=32, lora_alpha=32.
Dataset text describes the format filter inconsistently (start uppercase or end with punctuation) vs code (both required).
Multi-turn preference data unsupported by major libraries 'at the time of writing' (2024).
Only DPO is implemented; the RLHF/PPO comparison is asserted without citations to results.
Data sizes (100 to 10k etc.) are uncited rules of thumb.
practices: Apply the same quality principles as instruction data (accuracy, diversity, complexity) to preference data (Understanding preference datasets).
Keep the rejected answer meaningful; it encodes the behavior to remove (Preference data).
Prefer pairwise ranking over absolute scoring for LLM judges; add a ground-truth answer or grading note and chain of thought (Evaluating preferences).
Mitigate judge bias by randomizing A/B order, few-shot balanced examples and a multi-model jury (Evaluating preferences).
When a ground-truth human text exists, use it as chosen and an LLM output as rejected, skipping a judge (Creating our own preference dataset).
Use light DPO for style imitation: low learning rate, few epochs, higher beta (Implementing DPO).
With LoRA/QLoRA use ref_model=None so only one model is loaded (Implementing DPO).
Monitor training loss, validation loss, gradient norm, chosen/rejected rewards, margins and accuracies; 100% accuracy early signals easy pairs (Implementing DPO).
Iterate on the generation prompt with manual evaluation (Creating our own preference dataset).
